chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: Why the old brass bands used no piano
summary: Bands used bass, guitar, banjo and drum, with trombone, clarinet and cornet in set roles, as with Kid Ory and Preston Jackson.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Where would they come to play, Danny?
Where would they come to play?
They'd go out on the corner, to the corner and stop, and play on the corner.
Well, of course, you couldn't use a piano there, because you're on the wagon, huh?

On the wagon... But I mean, the bands, as a rule, never used a piano, because it just was a good sounding thing. A bass, a good guitar and a banjo and a drum, with a good-sized drum that had a boom to it, which was tuned. And it was a sound that was fascinating, because you had the (?) marching, a trombonist that could play. The trombone, the clarinet and the cornet playing the melody, and the trombone giving them the slide...
You could hear Kid Ory's mute(?); him and Preston Jackson did that to perfection.

They knew where to come in there, and don't get no (?) on a man's note. The clarinet would just noodle around, and would make the filigrees all around -- don't touch that melody. And you'd watch that, and you'd hear the rhythm with that guitar. Good guitar players, generally, and good banjo players then had the figure-eight stroke. They kept a rhythm going in there, stating that beat. And that big bass drum had a good sound. And the bass player that had a (?) bass that played, you know, the... Well, you had something there.
